q: You need a spreadsheet formula but don't remember the syntax. What is the skill the lesson wants you to build?
options: Memorising the most common formula names
Describing the job clearly in plain English and letting AI write it
Building the spreadsheet by hand to stay in control
explanation: The skill isn't knowing =TEXT() by heart; it's describing what you want clearly enough for AI to translate. AI gives you the formula, the cell references and an explanation — then you test it on a few rows before trusting it.

q: You want to upload a company spreadsheet to ChatGPT and ask questions about it. What should you do first?
options: Upload the original so the answers are accurate
Send the file link instead of the file
Upload only the columns you care about
Use a copy with anything sensitive removed
explanation: Upload a copy with anything sensitive removed, and treat the answers as a starting point rather than an audit. Keeping the raw data safe is one of the day's rules.

q: AI gives you a formula and a forecast model. What is the one rule the lesson repeats?
options: Verify every number against a value you already know
Never question a number AI produces
Only use models built from your own data
Ask AI to audit its own work first
explanation: AI can be confidently wrong about numbers, so check every formula against a value you already know. Verification is the rule that turns AI's fast first pass into something you can rely on.
